content: **List of Contents** Graphic 3D Pattern Add Graphic **Graphic（3D Pattern）** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kBwCxa7kb4Y \- Add Graphics to 3D Garments in the 3D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022458008/mceclip0.png) **Graphic** (**3D Pattern)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Material ▶ Graphic ▶ **Graphic**(**3D Pattern)** ** Add Graphic** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zJZZB058Xig \- When the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022458008/mceclip0.png) **Graphic(3D Pattern)** tool is selected, the File Browser will appear. \- Select the image file to be added. title: Deactivate (Pattern Only)
content: **List of Contents** Deactivate (Pattern Only) Result of Deactivate (Pattern Only) Features of Deactivate (Pattern Only) **Deactivate (Pattern Only)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y9KRz0vrvPA \- Deactivate selected Patterns to easily perform meticulous editing on the 3D Garment. \- Select desired Patterns to be deactivated and right click to access the pop-up menu. Then, select **Deactivate (Pattern Only).** ** Result of Deactivate (Pattern Only)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tC9MUU71wJo \- When the selected Patterns are properly deactivated, Patterns should turn translucent navy. When the Simulation is activated, deactivated Patterns will not move, but sewing lines will still be activated. \- To activate the selected Patterns, right click again and select **Activate.** **Features of Deactivate (Pattern Only)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sXaQFp_QEN0 \- Deactivated Patterns will not be calculated for collision. \- Simulate overlapped Patterns, one being activated and the other being deactivated. The activated Pattern will easily pass through the deactivated Pattern. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to deactivate patterns in 3D garment editing, including step-by-step instructions, visual aids, and details on the resulting effects and features of the deactivation process.

title: Apply Linked Editing – Symmetry Pattern (with Sewing)
content: **List of Contents** Symmetry Pattern (with Sewing) Apply Symmetry Pattern (with Sewing) Remove Symmetry Pattern (with Sewing) **Symmetry Pattern (with Sewing)** \- Edit identical Patterns symmetrically at the same, including their Sewing Lines. ** Apply Symmetry Pattern (with Sewing)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzRfxVV4fJY \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png)**Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. \- Right-click on the Patterns to be linked and select Apply Linked Editing – **Symmetry Pattern (with Sewing)** from the pop-up menu. \- The symmetrized Patterns will be highlighted in blue. \- The symmetrized Patterns can be edited symmetrically at the same time. **Remove Symmetry Pattern (with Sewing)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BTNRHvVdD5c \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. \- Right-click on the Patterns to be unlinked and select **Remove Linked Editing** from the pop-up menu. \- The symmetrized Patterns will be separated. \- The Patterns can be edited individually. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to create, apply, and remove symmetry patterns in sewing, complete with instructional videos and step-by-step tools for efficient editing.

title: Deactivate(Pattern & Sewing)/Activate
content: ### **Objective** Deactivated Patterns are considered as nonexistence in the 3D window. Therefore the rest of the Patterns simulate through the deactivated Patterns. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490267/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ **Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing)** / **Activate** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490287/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) Transform Pattern ▶ 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ **Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing)** / **Activate** → The selected Patterns and connected Sewing Lines are now being deactivated/activated.

title: Offset Pattern Outline
content: **Offset Pattern Outline** * **Offset Pattern Outline ** \- Extend the Pattern outline while maintaining the shape of the Pattern. * **Offset a Segment ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=89K2uzTOe4c \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022571447/mceclip0.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a segment of a Pattern and select **Offset Pattern Outline** from the pop-up menu. \- The Offset Pattern Outline Window will appear. * **Distance** : set how much the Offset Pattern Outline will be apart from the original Pattern outline. * **Number of Offsets** : set how many offsets will be duplicated. * **Total Distance** : total distance equals to the result of Distance multiplying Number of Offsets. * **Create Internal Line** : toggle on to convert the original Pattern outline as an Internal Line. * **Extend Side Segments** : toggle on the option to extend adjacent Pattern outlines, maintaining their original slope. * **Default Corner, Right Angled Corner, and Unfilled Corner** : decide how corners of the offset Pattern outline will be shaped. This option is not used when offsetting a segment. * **Offset an Entire Pattern ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_93HaonYlfQ \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022571447/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022571767/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a Pattern and select **Offset Pattern Outline** from the pop-up menu. \- The Offset Pattern Outline Window will appear. * **Distance** : set how much the Offset Pattern Outline will be apart from the original pattern outline. * **Number of Offsets** : set how many offsets will be duplicated. * **Total Distance** : total distance equals to the result of Distance multiplying Number of Offsets. * **Create Internal Line** : toggle on to convert the original Pattern outline as an Internal Line. * **Extend Side Segments** : toggle on the option to extend adjacent Pattern outlines, maintaining their original slope. This is not used when offsetting an entire Pattern. * **Default Corner, Right Angled Corner, and Unfilled Corner** : decide how corners of the offset Pattern outline will be shaped. The Pattern outline will be offset based on the setting.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to effectively use the Offset Pattern Outline feature to extend and customize pattern outlines while preserving their original shapes in your design workflow.

title: [3D Tool] Segment Sewing
content: ### **Objective** In the 3D window, easily establish Sewing Lines on segments of Patterns or Internal Shapes/Lines. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Segment Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001250948/_______.png) **Segment Sewing** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Segment Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001250948/_______.png) **Segment Sewing ** → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Navigate to the 3D window. 3. Click once on the Pattern Outline to establish the first half of the seam. 4. With the mouse cursor, hover over the segment to be sewn to the first half of the seam. → When moving the mouse cursor, a blue point appears indicating the length of the first half of the seam. 5. When the mouse cursor is moved close to the blue point, the Sewing Line snaps to the point (ver5.1.0). Drag the mouse to make the the Directional Notches parallel to each other. Then, click to establish the second half of the seam. **※ Note** * When Directional Notches are crossed, the Sewing Lines in the 3D window are crossed as well. When Patterns are simulated at this state, either one of the Patterns is reversed and then sewn to the other Pattern. * Use the shortcut to establish M:N Sewing Lines. For more detail, please reference [M:N Segment Sewing](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001771067).
content_description: Learn how to efficiently establish Sewing Lines on segments of Patterns or Internal Shapes in both 2D and 3D windows using the Segment Sewing tool.

title: Edit Notch Properties
content: **List of Contents** Notch Properties Edit Notch Properties Notch Length **Notch Properties YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yt0bkOa9zaA ** \- Edit properties of a Notch as needed. \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026559547/mceclip0.png) **Notch** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Notch** ** Edit Notch Properties YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lRYwtK0Uw6U ** \- Select the Notch to be modified. \- The properties of the selected Notch appear in the Property Editor. * **Name YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1nwU8XVE3EU **\- Rename the Notch. * **Type YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Iz3kah5lC28 ** \- Choose the type of the Notch. * **Angle YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B6dieNf2Ynw ** \- Set the degree of angle for the Notch. * **Perpendicular** \- The Notch is placed perpendicular to its segment. * **Custom** \- Decide the angle of the Notch based on its segment. * **Direction YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=te-WS1ugNxQ ** \- This option only appears when a Notch is created in a corner. \- Decided the direction of the Notch. * **Point (Center)** \- The Notch is created at the center of the corner. * **Segment 1** \- The Notch is created towards a segment. * **Segment 2** \- The Notch is created towards the other segment. * **Flip YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YIk80LPWgQ8 ** \- The Notch is created on the other side of the segment. **Notch Length_ver.5.0.0 and Above** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V5GvUlF-xxQ \- Edit Notch length as desired. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for editing and customizing notch properties in your design software, complete with instructional videos for each feature.

title: Delete Notch

title: Notch
content: **List of Contents** Notch Create Notch Select Notch Move Notch Delete Notch Notch on Seam Allowance Notch Display Type **Notch YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3ey_Nu931a8 ** \- Create, select, move, and delete Notches on Pattern outlines. \- Select the Notch tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Notch** ** Create Notch** * **Create Manually YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sGcWMX3P-Hg ** \- Hover the mouse over the Pattern outline or Internal Line where a notch should be added. \- A red point appears on the segment where the mouse is hovering over. \- Click on the segment to create a Notch and it is automatically selected and highlighted in yellow. * **Create with Specific Numbers YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CHHpoggTkYU ** \- To create a Notch on a specific position, right click on a segment where a notch is desired to be added. \- The Notch window appears allowing you to specify location. * **Split into Two Lines ** \- The line will be divided into two lines based on the reference point which was created when you hover the mouse over and right click the segment. The shorter side is indicated as **Line 1** , and the longer side is indicated as **Line 2.** \- The ratio of the line to be split is 100%. The line can be divided into two lines based on the ratio. Enter the desired ratio in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. * **Split by Length** \- Divide the selected line into multiple segments according to the desired length of each segment. \- **Segment Length** : Enter the segment length, which the whole line should be divided according to the interval. To reverse the direction that points are added, select Reverse Direction. \- **Number of Segments** : Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. \- **Direction** : Reverse the direction that points are added. * **Uniform Split** \- Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into next to the **Number of Segments** option. The line is equally divided accordingly. **Select Notch YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O-A0_lHdZEc ** \- Click the Notch created on a segment. \- The Notch is selected and highlighted in yellow. **Move Notch** * **Move Manually YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iAoHhC1msM0 ** \- Click and drag the Notch created on a Pattern outline or an Internal Line. \- Release the mouse when the Notch is moved to the desired place. \- The Notch is successfully moved. * **Move with Specific Numbers YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lvx84ARiQAU ** \- To move the Notch with specific numbers, right click while click-and-dragging the Notch. \- Enter the desired value when the Moving Distance window appears. 。 \- The Notch is moved accordingly. **Delete Notch YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TZRfWUd-dAg ** \- Select the Notch to be deleted. \- Hit the Delete key on the keyboard. \- Or, right click on the Notch to be deleted and select Delete option from the pop-up menu. **Notch on Seam Allowance_ver5.0.0 and Above ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r_DqnNjxrIg \- When a notch is added, it appears on both its Pattern Outline and the seam allowance. \- When a seam allowance is added to a Pattern Outline with a notch, the notch appears on the seam allowance as well. \- When a notch is added to a corner with seam allowance, the notch randomly appears on either side of the seam allowance at the corner. **Notch Display Type_ver5.0.0 and Above ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PMnlgJ7qzY0 \- Configure notches' 2D display options. \- Navigate to the path: Main Menu ▶ Setting ▶ User Setting ▶ 2Dㅁ ▶ **Notch** * **Length Fixed to Screen** : Notches are displayed in a fixed length regardless of the screen size (zoom in or out.) ※Note: When this option is selected, the **Notch Length** option disappears from the Property Editor. * **Actual Length** : Notches's size adapts to the screen size (zoom in or out.) ※Note : When this option is selected, the Notch Length option appears in the Property Editor. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for users to learn how to create, select, move, and delete notches on pattern outlines, complete with instructional videos and detailed steps.

title: Internal Ellipse
content: **List of Contents** Internal Ellipse Create **Internal EllipseYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_0FCRmB9heg ** \- Create ellipse or circle within a Pattern. \- Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Ellipse** \- 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Shape_Inner_Circle.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001203908/Toolbar_2D_Shape_Inner_Circle.png)**Internal Ellipse** **Create** * **Create**** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TTXryZsJjpU** \- Click and drag within a Pattern to create an ellipse in the 2D window. \- To create a circle, hold down the Shift key while click and drag. * **Create with Specific ValuesYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4jKzfBVvA2k** \- Click within a Pattern to create an ellipse with specific values. \- The Create Ellipse window appears. * Size Diameter: Set width and height of an ellipse. Radius: Set width and height of the radius of an ellipse. Circumference: Set overall circumference of an ellipse. * Replicate Interval : Set the distance between each replicated ellipses. Angle : Set the angle between each replicated ellipses. Number of Shapes : Set the number of ellipses to be replicated. * Position Outline : Configure the ellipse’s location by setting the ellipse outline’s offset from the Pattern outlines’ left, right, top, and bottom. Center : Configure the ellipse’s location by setting the ellipse center’s offset from the Pattern outlines’ left, right, top, and bottom. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating internal ellipses and circles within a pattern, featuring step-by-step instructions, specific value settings, and instructional YouTube videos.

title: Create Custom Texture Image
content: **List of Contents** Scan Fabric Create Repeat Match DPI (Resolution) Match Color **Objective** Create various custom texture images and apply to fabrics to express variety of fabric in CLO. There are four steps total to create a custom texture image: Scanning Fabric, Making Repeat, Matching DPI (Resolution), and Adjusting Color. In order to make custom texture image, image editing software, such as [Pixplant](https://www.pixplant.com/index.php), [Adobe Photoshop](http://www.adobe.com/products/photoshop.html) is needed. **Operation** **Scan Fabric** Scan fabrics to digitize real world fabrics. If scanner is not available, use digital camera or cellphone camera instead. 1. Prepare the scanner, digital camera, or cellphone camera. 2. Spread the fabric flat on an even surface and photograph it, aligning the grainline perpendicular to the scanner or the camera's corner of the screen. 3. Send the image to the computer. **Create Repeat ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3bf4ZCaMQeo When a fabric is observed carefully, you can find the structure which repeats like a pattern and the structure of the fabric is often indicated as a Repeat. To express a fabric's texture, create a Repeat using the scanned image. Ways to create a Repeat differs depending on the characteristics of each fabric. Please refer to the appropriate guideline as needed. **When Fabric Structure is Small and Irregular** 1. Launch [PixPlant](https://www.pixplant.com/download.php). If PixPlant is not available, please use other image editing software such as Adobe Photoshop. 2. Left click on the Add button on the right top corner and locate the scanned image to load. 3. Left click on the Straighten Seed > Click to Edit button, then select a clean part of the scanned image. 4. Click the Generate button to create a Repeat. 5. The area inside the square box in the Texture Canvas window represents the Repeat. Repeat procedure 3 and 4 until the desired Repeat is achieved. 6. To recreate some portion of the Repeat, drag to select the desired part within the square box in the Texture Canvas window. 7. When the desired Repeat is achieved, click Save. **When Fabric Structure is Big and Regular** 1. Launch [Adobe Photoshop](http://www.adobe.com/products/photoshop.html) or other image editing software. 2. Find the smallest repeated area on the scanned image. 3. Select and cut the repeated area. 4. Copy, paste and align repeated area to check if they align naturally. 5. When the repeated area does not align properly, showing grid lines, edit the image to make it align more smoothly. 6. When the desired image is achieved, save the image. **※ Note:** When creating Repeats for fabrics with transparency, please select and delete the Repeat image's background and save it as PNG. **Match DPI (Resolution)** In order to match the image ratio of the Repeat and the real world fabric, adjust DPI (Resolution). 1. Launch Adobe Photoshop. 2. Open previously created Repeat. 3. Navigate and select Main Menu > Image > Image Size. 4. When a pop-up window appears, toggle on the Resample Image option and adjust the DPI (Resoultion) value respective to the DPI (Resolution) of the original scanned image. Open the original scanned image in Adobe Photoshop to check its DPI (Resolution) value. 5. Save the Repeat. **Match Color** Match the Repeat's color respective to the real world fabric. Occasionally, photographing fabric may distort the fabric's real color. In these cases, after creating a Repeat image, adjust its color, matching the color to the original fabric's color. Open the Repeat in an image editing software such as Adobe Photoshop and adjust color as needed. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for creating custom texture images from scanned fabrics, detailing the essential steps of scanning, creating repeats, matching DPI, and adjusting colors using image editing software.

title: How can I express embroidery in CLO?
content: **Question** How can I express embroidery in CLO? **Answer** There are three possible ways to express embroidery in CLO differ by the purpose and the situation. With Scanned Embroidery Without Scanned Embroidery** ** **With Scanned Embroidery** When there is a scanned image of embroidery, use the [Graphic tools](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000483967) in CLO to express embroidery. However, as expressing thick embroidery and flat embroidery methods are different, please refer to the appropriate guide below. ** Express Embroidery with Thickness ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=unFS2e09qd8 To express embroidery with thickness, please refer to below instruction. 1. [Create](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000511208) a rectangle Pattern in the 2D window. 2. Apply a new fabric to the Pattern and add texture. 3. [Create Internal Lines](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000481707) in the shape of embroidery on the Pattern and cut. 4. Delete unnecessary Pattern and duplicate the Pattern outline as an Internal Shape to the 3D Garment Pattern. 5. [Sew](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000641848-%EC%9E%AC%EB%B4%89%EC%84%A0-%EC%83%9D%EC%84%B1) the embroidery Pattern to the 3D Garment. 6. Click on the fabric item applied to the embroidery Pattern in the Object Browser and change its Preset as Fusible Rigid. Also, change the Particle Distance to 5. ** Express Flat Embroidery ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cII93rWvu3M Use the [Graphic tools](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000483967) to add the embroidery image to the 3D Garment in order to express embroidery with no thickness. **Without Scanned Embroidery **** **If there is no scanned image of embroidery, use the image editing tool such as Adobe Photoshop to express embroidery effects. Then, refer to guides from the With Scanned Embroidery section. You may search how to express embroidery in image editing tools online or take a look at the reference we found below! [Video Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HbZac9imfZA) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Discover various methods to express embroidery in CLO, whether using scanned images or creating effects from scratch.

title: Create Custom Texture Image for Curved Pattern
content: **List of Contents** Using Adobe Photoshop Using Adobe Illustrator **Objective** Create custom texture image for curved pattern such as neckband. Use curved texture image when expressing lace or biz trims. **Operation** **Using Adobe Photoshop ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jte2rUXzrIw Create custom texture image for curved pattern in Adobe Photoshop. 1. [Create a Repeat](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012228067) of real world fabric. 2. Open the pattern file which the custom texture image will be applied to. 3. Right click on the curved pattern which the custom texture image will be applied to, then select Zoom to Selected on the pop-up menu. 4. Take a screenshot of the pattern. 5. Launch Adobe Photoshop and open both screenshot and Repeat image. 6. Place the Repeat image on top of the pattern image. 7. Use the [Warp](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/using/warp-images-shapes-paths.html) function to transform the Repeat image respective to the pattern. 8. Open a new window in Adobe Photoshop. 9. Select, copy, and paste the modified Repeat image to the newly opened window. 10. Save the modified Repeat image as PNG and be mindful to set the canvas size bigger than the modified Repeat image for easy application and modification in CLO. 11. [Apply](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000471388) the modified Repeat image to the pattern and [adjust](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002680348) as needed to place the graphic properly. **Using Adobe Illustrator ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C2b2OfG33V8 **** Create custom texture image for curved pattern in Adobe Illustrator. 1. [Create a Repeat](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012228067) of real world fabric. 2. Open the pattern file which the custom texture image will be applied to. 3. Right click on the curved pattern which the custom texture image will be applied to, then select Zoom to Selected on the pop-up menu. 4. Take a screenshot of the pattern. 5. Launch Adobe Illustrator and open both screenshot and Repeat image. 6. Trace the pattern image with the [pen](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/drawing-pen-curvature-or-pencil.html) tool. 7. Select the Repeat image and [add as a pattern brush](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/how-to/illustrator-create-pattern-brush.html). 8. Select and copy the longest segment of the traced pattern and apply the pattern brush created in procedure 6. 9. Place the traced pattern on top of the segment with pattern brush applied. 10. Select both pattern and segment, right click and select Make Clipping Mask. The segment with pattern brush applied will be clipped based on the pattern shape. 11. Select the clipped pattern, navigate and select Main Menu > File > Export Selection. 12. Designate the saving path, file name and save as PNG. 13. [Apply](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000471388) the modified Repeat image to the pattern and [adjust](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002680348) as needed to place the graphic properly. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for creating custom texture images for curved patterns, specifically for neckbands and trims, using Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator.

title: Garment Rendering Style
content: **List of Contents** Garment Rendering Style Textured Surface Thick Textured Surface Transparent Surface Monochrome Surface Mesh Random Colored Surface **Garment Rendering Style** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5GcJjTtVxhk \- Check the tightness of 3D Garments with the color scale. \- Hover over the third icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu in the 3D window. ** Textured Surface** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=smqtYtFzLPs \- Only the front side of the 3D Garment will appear in its original color and the back side will appear darker to indicate the sides of the fabric. \- The Garment thickness will not be expressed. **Thick Textured Surface** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Z-FXrLR7Yk \- Both front and back sides of the 3D Garment will appear in their original color and the Garment thickness will be expressed. **Transparent Surface** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2GCZ6r3TPgI \- The 3D Garment will turn translucent. **Monochrome Surface** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3hg2aA4YMvc \- The 3D Garment will appear in black and white. \- The Garment thickness will not be expressed. **Mesh** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JUPrj9c6mGM \- The 3D Garment will appear in the mesh structure. **Random Color Surface_ver5.0.0 and Above** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cK1d2Ohd5E0 \- Select the **Random Color Surface** icon to distinguish Patterns as they are assigned to random colors. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore various garment rendering styles through informative videos, showcasing techniques to visualize 3D garments with different textures, colors, and effects.

Navigate to Print Layout mode. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ **Edit Texture ** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![edit_texture.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024350388/edit_texture.png) **Edit Texture ** 3. Select the Fabric with the print/texture to be edited. → The selected Fabric print/texture properties appear in the Property Editor. 4. Or, use the **in** and **mm** options to insert desired value. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ **Edit Texture ** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![edit_texture.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024350388/edit_texture.png) **Edit Texture** ** ** 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ **Edit Texture ** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![edit_texture.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024350388/edit_texture.png) **Edit Texture** ** ** 3. title: Garment Information

title: Edit Binding Properties

title: Adjust Stretch-Weft/Warp, Shear
content: ### **Objective** Use the **Weft** , **Warp** and **Shear** intensities to show the resistance against the horizontal, vertical and diagonal elasticity according to the 2D window. Increasing the **Shear** intensity to the same ratio as the **Weft** and **Warp** intensities, is going to express materials that creases easily such as cotton and denim. On the other hand, decreasing the intensity value is going to express more elastic materials such as silk and jersey. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Stretch-Weft** /**Warp** , **Shear** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005548088/______.png)
content_description: Explore how adjusting Weft, Warp, and Shear intensities in the Fabric Property Editor influences the elasticity and crease resistance of various materials in a 2D window.

title: Edit Binding Properties
content: **List of Contents** Binding Properties Edit Binding Properties **Binding Properties** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vonEOlpfYzQ \- Adjust properties for Binidngs. ** ** \- Select the ![edit_binding.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001829187/edit_binding.jpg)**Select Binding** tool from the 3D toolbar. **※****Note: ** Binding can also be selected with the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. ** Edit Binding Properties** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkwZzbESthw \- When the Binding tool is selected, the 3D garment turns translucent and segments with Binding appear in grey. \- Select the Binding to be edited. \- Selected Binding’s properties appear in the Property Editor. * Name : Rename Binding’s name. * Type: Place the Binding below or above the Pattern. * Line Length: Check Binding’s length. However, it cannot be changed from the Property Editor. * Width (mm): Adjust selected Binding’s width (1~30mm). * Length (%): Adjust selected Binding's length with percentage (50~200%) (ver5.0.0.) * Length (in): Adjust selected Binding's length with a specific value. When adjusting the Binding with a specific value, the unit follows the program's default unit (ver5.0.0.) * Particle Distance (mm): Edit selected Binding’s Particle Distance (1~20mm). * Add'l Thickness - Collision (mm): Adjust the **Add'l Thickness - Collision** value of each Binding (ver5.0.0.) * Fabric: Assign Fabric to the Binding. * Fabric styles in the Fabric Object Browser appear in a list. * Topstitch: Apply Topstitch on top of the Binding. All Topstitch styles added in the Object Browser appear as options (ver4.2.0.) * Sewing Line Type: Edit Binding’s Sewing Line Type. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on editing binding properties in a 3D garment design, complete with instructional videos and detailed steps for adjusting various binding attributes.

content: **Objective** Use this function to adjust the friction of Garments. title: [Style Property] Apply Topstitch Texture
content: ### Objective Change texture type for Topstitch(es). **※ Note :** Texture can only be applied when the type is selected for Texture in the Property Editor. **Location** Property Editor ▶ Texture ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005672048/__.png) **Search** **Operation** 1. Object Browser ▶ Select a Topstitch to add texture image. → The selected Topstitch is now being highlighted. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor ▶ Texture ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005672048/__.png) **Search** → The Open File window appears. 3. Select and open desired texture image file. → The selected image is now being applied to the selected Topstitch. **※ Note :** Not like fabrics, texture image file cannot be applied by Drag & Drop for Topstitch.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to change the texture type for Topstitch(es) in the Property Editor of CLO 3D.

title: Elastic
content: ### List of Contents Pattern Pattern Outline or Internal Line ### Objective Apply elastic to the patterns or lines to express details such as E-bands or shirring. ### Operation #### **Pattern (ver 7.2)** 1. In the Library window, click Fabric » Elastic folder. 2. In the fabric tab of the Object Browser, select the fabric of the pattern to represent E-band. → Property Editor appears. 3. Click the Elastic option on the right side of the Physical Property. → Elastic properties appear. 4. Adjust the Elastic properties. | Preset | Set the default elastic presets. ---|--- Strength and Stiffness | Adjust the strength and stiffness of the elastic. Thickness | Set the thickness of the elastic. #### **Pattern Outline or Internal Line** 1. Select a outer or internal line with ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005538548/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png)**Edit Pattern** tool. → Property Editor appears. 2. Click the Elastic option to **On**. 3. Adjust the Elastic properties. Strength | Adjust the strength of the elastic. ---|--- Ratio | Adjust the ratio of the elastic. Segment Length | Adjusts the elastic ratio when the length value is entered. Total Length | If multiple segments are selected, the entered value will be applied as the total length of the combined segments.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions on how to apply elastic properties to patterns and lines in design software, enabling users to effectively create E-bands and shirring effects.

title: Opacity
content: **Opacity** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vi7yKxvRnBk \- Adjust the **Opacity** to express see-through materials. \- Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and adjust Material ▶ **Opacity.** \- Adjust the scrollbar or type in desired values to edit the Opacity values. \- The material’s Opacity will change according to the setting.
content_description: Explore how to adjust the opacity of materials in your designs by following our step-by-step guide, featuring a helpful YouTube video tutorial.
